TLIC: Learned Image Compression with ROI-Weighted
Distortion and Bit Allocation
Wei Jiang1, Yongqi Zhai1,2, Hangyu Li1, Ronggang Wang1,2,3∗
1Shenzhen Graduate School, Peking University
2Pengcheng Laboratory
3Migu Culture Technology Co., Ltd
jiangwei@stu.pku.edu.cn
rgwang@pkusz.edu.cn
Abstract
This short paper describes our method for the track of image compression. To achieve better
perceptual quality, we use the adversarial loss to generate realistic textures, use region of
interest (ROI) mask to guide the bit allocation for diﬀerent regions. Our Team name is
TLIC.
1
Introduction
Learned image compression [1] becomes an active area in recent years. Some of the
models [2–6] have outperformed latest non-learned codec VVC. Most of the methods
focus on non-perceptual metric optimization. To improve perceptual quality, some
methods [7–9] employ Generative Adversial Networks (GANs) [10] to generate percep-
tual textures. In addition, VGG[11] or LPIPS[12]-based learned metrics are employed
to help convergence. Since people have diﬀerent standards for subjective criterion,
for some content sensitive images, such as faces, documents, keeping its authenticity
is more important than generating vivid but fake texture. To this end, in this paper,
based on the generative image compression framework [8], we propose Learned Image
Compression with ROI-Weighted Distortion and Bit Allocation, named TLIC. We
employ ROI to adjust the weight of the symbols in the latent to allocate more bits
to regions of interest. In addition, to enhance the guidance, we employ roi mask to
control the weight of distortion of each pixels. At last, to satisfy target bits, our
model is trained with a variable rate compression method inspired from [13].
2
Method
2.1
Overview
In this section, we brieﬂy introduce our method for perceptual image compression.
The architecture of our TLIC is similar to Ma et al. [14]. The gain and inverse gain
units [13] are employed for variable rate control.
The optimization process of our TLIC contains two stages. In the ﬁrst stage, the
model is optimized for mean-square-error (MSE) with gain and inverse gain units.
During the sencond stage, the model is optimized for perceptual quality.

For perceptual quality optimization, we adopt adversarial loss [10] [7][8] to guide
the decoder to generate realistic textures at low bit-rate. Our discriminator employs
the Unet [15] architecture. In addition to adversarial loss, we used L1 loss to keep
the texture sharp. LPIPS loss [12] and Style loss [16] are also used to enhance the
quality. We also use the Laplacian loss [17] to reduced color variation. Following [14],
we use a region of interest (ROI) mask to guide the network to allocate more bits in
regions of interest. The overall loss function is

2.2
ROI-Weighted Distortion and Bit Allocation
In our method, following Ma et al. [14], we employ saliency map as the ROI map
because the saliency detection can distinguish the image into the focused area and
background, which is more suitable to our strategy. We employ the RMformer [18] to
generate ROI maps. The RMformer is ﬁxed during training and testing. The process
is formulated as:
Mask2D = sigmoid(RMformer(x)),
(2)

further pooled to smooth the boundaries for smooth bit-allocation.
RM2D = AvgPool(Mask2D),

of the ROI in terms of rate allocation. What’s more, we protect a certain number of
channels to retain appropriate information for the background to avoid the fading of
its reconstructed texture. Finally, the bit-allocation is achieved at the encoder side
and can be formulated as:

2.3
Adversial Training
To generate realistic textures, we employ the adversarial loss to optimize the model.
Following existing methods [8, 14], we employ BCE loss. The loss function is formu-
lated as:
Dadv = E(−log(D(ˆy, ˆx)),
Ddisc = E(−log(1 −D(ˆy, ˆx)) + E(−log(D(ˆy, x)),
(5)
where D is the discriminator. Ddisc is employed to optimize the descriminator. We
employ the U-net discriminator [15] for more accurate pixel-wise feedback while main-
taining syntax feedback.
2.4
Variable Rate Adaptation
The gain units and inverse gain units are employed for continuous rate adaptation.
Speciﬁcally, the model is trained for n target bit-rates. The gain units MG ∈Rc×n
is employed to adjust the quantization step of each channel,where c is the channel
number of each channel. The inverse gain is 1/MG in our model. The process in

2.5
Entropy Model
The entropy model is a simpliﬁed version of recent linear complexity multi-reference
entropy model [5]. The latent residual prediction modules [19] and the inter-slice
global context modules are removed to reduce model parameters and we employ one
layer convolution-based local context modules. The number of slices are set to 5.
2.6
Training
To accelerate the training, 320 × 320 patches are employed during training and the
batch size is set 8.
3
Conclusion
In this report, we propose to employ the ROI-weighted rate allocation and distortion
for better perceptual quality. To enhance the pixel feedback and syntax feedback of
adversarial optimization, we employ the U-net based discriminator architecture. To
achieve the target bit-rate, we employ the gain units and inverse gain units.
